text:
alex: noticing a big throughput collapse in prod-us-west GPU pool, started ~03:15UTC. p50 OK but tps down ~60%, some workers restarting. getting repeated `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` in logs.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (prod-us-west throughput regression) — tagging oncall.

maya: saw the same, logs show a lot of small `cuMemAlloc` failures followed by worker exit. attaching snippet in a sec.

dev-runtime: paste: ```
[nodename: gpu-node-17] Worker 82: runtime: allocate failed: cuMemAlloc(0x3f200000) -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[...stack...] runtime/allocator.py:237 evict_candidate -> false
```

jen: can we get `nvidia-smi` and `pmap` for the process? I want to see fragmentation vs total usage.

dev-runtime: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv` -> 
"memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB]
12040, 8347
"

dev-runtime: also gc metrics: `kv_cache_entries` shot up 3x around incident start. KV size per worker went from ~120MB -> ~540MB for some requests (long contexts).

_tomas_: I pulled a flamegraph from the runtime profiler for affected worker — looks like repeated `cudaMalloc`/`cudaFree` churn when kernel selection falls back to the reference kernels for certain attention config. Fallback seems to trigger larger allocation footprints and prevents the allocator from reusing slabs.

jen: that matches the allocator logs I saw — slab pools show heavy fragmentation, free lists full of tiny holes. We have many small KV allocations mixed with big transient buffers; coalescing isn't happening.

alex: what changed recently? any kernel selection rollout?

_tomas_: yes, at 02:30UTC we enabled kernel-routing heuristic v2 (tries experimental fused kernels for long sequences). There's a fallback path that exercises a different allocation pattern. I suspect v2 + long-context requests = fragmentation + high freq cuMemAlloc attempts.

_maya_: also noticed an uptick in cross-tenant traffic to that pool around the same time — possible noisy neighbor amplifying fragmentation.

_sre-lead_: OK immediate mitigations: 1) disable kernel-routing v2 for prod-us-west (rollback flag), 2) trigger rolling restart of pool nodes to drain and reclaim allocator arenas, 3) throttle long-context KV retention for the hot route. Any objections?

jen: thumbs up to rollback. Also we can set `CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` temporarily to reduce large-slab allocation behavior (low risk) and reduce fragmentation.

dev-runtime: applying rollback flag -> `feature.kernel_routing_v2=false` on prod-us-west. Pushing config now.

ci-bot: Deploy triggered: rollout-config/prod-us-west at 03:47UTC by dev-runtime.

10m later

maya: after the flag flip, `cuMemAlloc` failures dropped significantly but there are still a handful of restarts. starting rolling restart of 10 nodes with graceful drain.

alex: running quick KV eviction script to bound growth on hot routes: `redis-cli EVAL "return redis.call('del', KEYS[1])" 1 kv:route:hot:*` (targeted, small blast).

dev-runtime: restarted nodes 3/10, memory reclaimed, tps bumping to ~85% of baseline.

_tomas_: profiler after mitigation shows allocator reuse is working again, fragmentation index down from 0.63 -> 0.18. flamegraph attached: major reduction in `cuMemAlloc` walltime.

jen: left a note: follow-up actions — add guardrail to kernel-routing that prevents fallback path for pools with < X free allocator slabs; add instrumentation for per-worker slab fragmentation; improve KV eviction heuristic for mixed-size workloads.

_sre-lead_: agreed. Also schedule a canary for kernel-routing v2 with synthetic long-context load to validate allocator behavior before enabling.

alex: final status — throughput recovered to ~96% of normal after restarts + config rollback. No more OOMs observed for 30m. Closing incident if stable. :thumbsup: :lock:

oncall-bot: INC-2026-042 updated: resolved at 04:05UTC. Postmortem assigned to tomas + jen.

jen: I'll own the follow-up; will file a short RFC on allocator guardrails and KV eviction tuning.

alex: thanks all. good catch on the kernel fallback + KV pattern.
